theorems.name: Arrow-Debreu State-Price Pricing: Linearity
theorems.description: Linear pricing functional `V_0(X + Y) = V_0(X) + V_0(Y)` from Arrow-Debreu state prices.

    (s : Finset ι) (q X Y : ι → ℝ) :
    MathFin.statePricePricing s q (fun i => X i + Y i) =
      MathFin.statePricePricing s q X + MathFin.statePricePricing s q Y :=

theorems.name: State Prices as Risk-Neutral Expectation
theorems.description: If q_i = e^{-rT} · ν_i where ν is the risk-neutral measure, then V_0(X) = e^{-rT} · E^ν[X].

code.lean:
import MathFin.Foundations.StatePrices

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory Real
open scoped NNReal
open MathFin

theorem statePricePricing_eq_riskNeutral_thm {ι : Type*}
    (s : Finset ι) (ν X : ι → ℝ) (rT : ℝ) :
    MathFin.statePricePricing s (fun i => Real.exp (-rT) * ν i) X =
      Real.exp (-rT) * ∑ i ∈ s, ν i * X i :=
  MathFin.statePricePricing_eq_riskNeutral s ν X rT

theorems.name: Triangle No-Arbitrage Determines the Third Rate
theorems.description: For positive exchange rates S_AB and S_BC (S_XY = units of Y per unit of X), exactly one rate S_CA leaves the three frictionless conversion trades A→B, B→C, C→A without arbitrage (no real combination whose net holding is non-negative in every currency and positive in one), namely S_CA = 1/(S_AB·S_BC). No-arbitrage is the multi-state FTAP's notion with the currencies as coordinates; reverse trades are at the reciprocal rate, and bid–ask spreads and transaction costs are not modelled.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Foundations.TriangleArbitrage

/-- **No arbitrage determines the third cross rate.** For positive `S_AB`, `S_BC` exactly one
    `S_CA` leaves the currency triangle without arbitrage, namely `1 / (S_AB · S_BC)`.
    Re-exports `MathFin.triangleNoArb_solve_third`. -/
theorem triangleNoArb_solve_third_thm {S_AB S_BC : ℝ} (h_ab : 0 < S_AB) (h_bc : 0 < S_BC) :
    ∃! S_CA : ℝ, MathFin.TriangleNoArb S_AB S_BC S_CA :=
  MathFin.triangleNoArb_solve_third h_ab h_bc

metadata.reference: Y. Aiba, N. Hatano, H. Takayasu, K. Marumo, T. Shimizu, Triangular arbitrage as an interaction among foreign exchange rates, Physica A 310 (2002) 467–479 (the rate product); H. Föllmer and A. Schied, Stochastic Finance: An Introduction in Discrete Time, 4th ed., de Gruyter (2016), §1.2
metadata.formalization_scope: Full formal proof. Re-export of MathFin.triangleNoArb_solve_third (MathFin/Foundations/TriangleArbitrage.lean). SCOPE: TriangleNoArb is defined as ¬ HasArbitrage_multi_state (triangleTrades S_AB S_BC S_CA), the multi-state FTAP's arbitrage over the currency coordinates, and triangleNoArb_iff proves it equivalent to S_AB·S_BC·S_CA = 1 for positive S_AB, S_BC. The hypotheses are positivity (not just non-vanishing): with a negative rate a single reversed trade is an arbitrage, so no S_CA works. Not modelled: bid–ask spreads, transaction costs.

theorems.name: Put-Call Parity from No-Arbitrage
theorems.description: Under a positive linear pricing functional (state prices q summing to the discount factor and pricing the spot), the call minus put portfolio is worth S0 - K*DF. First-principles parity, no distributional hypothesis.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Foundations.NoArbitrageDerivations

open MathFin

theorem putCall_parity_from_no_arbitrage_thm
    {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (q : ι → ℝ) (S : ι → ℝ)
    (DF S₀ K : ℝ)
    (h_bond : ∑ i ∈ s, q i = DF)
    (h_stock : ∑ i ∈ s, q i * S i = S₀) :
    (∑ i ∈ s, q i * max (S i - K) 0) - (∑ i ∈ s, q i * max (K - S i) 0)
      = S₀ - K * DF :=
  MathFin.putCall_parity_from_no_arbitrage s q S DF S₀ K h_bond h_stock

theorems.name: Forward Price from No-Arbitrage
theorems.description: Given state-price weights q that price the zero-coupon bond at DF ≠ 0 and the stock at S₀, exactly one forward strike F makes the forward contract's payoff S_T − F worth zero at inception. The statement asserts existence and uniqueness (∃!); the proof's witness is the cash-and-carry value F = S₀/DF, which the statement does not name.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Foundations.NoArbitrageDerivations

open MathFin

theorem forward_price_eq_spot_div_discount_thm
    {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (q : ι → ℝ) (S : ι → ℝ)
    (DF S₀ : ℝ) (hDF : DF ≠ 0)
    (h_bond : ∑ i ∈ s, q i = DF)
    (h_stock : ∑ i ∈ s, q i * S i = S₀) :
    ∃! F : ℝ, ∑ i ∈ s, q i * (S i - F) = 0 :=
  MathFin.forward_price_eq_spot_div_discount s q S DF S₀ hDF h_bond h_stock

theorems.name: Pricing Kernel: Butterfly No-Arbitrage from FTAP
theorems.description: In a two-state market, the FTAP-derived discounted state prices make call-price butterfly spreads cost ≥ 0 — the canonical static no-arbitrage constraint, derived not assumed.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Bridges.PricingKernel

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory

/-- **No-arbitrage ⟹ butterfly spreads cost ≥ 0** (Phase 53). For sign data
    `z_up > 0 > z_down`, the discounted FTAP state prices are non-negative, so the
    finite-state call-price functional `K ↦ Σᵢ qᵢ · max(Sᵢ − K, 0)` is convex in
    the strike and the butterfly combination `C(K₁) − 2·C((K₁+K₃)/2) + C(K₃)` has
    non-negative cost. The state prices come from the Phase 37 backward-FTAP EMM
    construction, so this static no-arbitrage constraint is derived, not assumed.
    Re-exports `MathFin.stateprice_call_butterfly_nonneg`. -/
theorem pricing_kernel_butterfly_nonneg
    (z_up z_down rT : ℝ) (h_up : 0 < z_up) (h_down : z_down < 0)
    (S : Fin 2 → ℝ) (K₁ K₃ : ℝ) :
    0 ≤ (∑ i, MathFin.statePrices_two_state z_up z_down rT i * max (S i - K₁) 0)
        - 2 * (∑ i, MathFin.statePrices_two_state z_up z_down rT i *
              max (S i - (K₁ + K₃) / 2) 0)
        + (∑ i, MathFin.statePrices_two_state z_up z_down rT i * max (S i - K₃) 0) :=
  MathFin.stateprice_call_butterfly_nonneg z_up z_down rT h_up h_down S K₁ K₃

theorems.name: Forward FTAP: Multi-State, Multi-Asset
theorems.description: EMM existence ⟹ no arbitrage in an arbitrary finite-state, finite-asset one-period market (forward Fundamental Theorem of Asset Pricing).

code.lean:
import MathFin.Foundations.FTAPMultiState

/-- **Forward FTAP, arbitrary finite state + finite assets** (Phase 42). If there
    is a strictly-positive probability `q` with `Σ q = 1` whose `q`-weighted excess
    return is zero for every asset (an equivalent martingale measure), then no
    portfolio attains a payoff that is non-negative in every state and strictly
    positive in at least one state — i.e. no arbitrage. Standard linearity /
    `Finset.sum_comm` argument. Re-exports `MathFin.noArbitrage_of_emm_multi`. -/
theorem ftap_multi_state_forward {N M : ℕ} (z : Fin M → Fin N → ℝ)
    (h_emm : MathFin.HasEMM_multi_state z) :
    ¬ MathFin.HasArbitrage_multi_state z :=
  MathFin.noArbitrage_of_emm_multi z h_emm

theorems.name: Cone-Separation Root (Convex-Duality Unification)
theorems.description: A closed convex cone in (ι → ℝ) disjoint from the standard simplex admits a strictly-positive functional that is ≤ 0 on the cone. This single geometric Hahn–Banach fact is the shared root of three apparently separate pillars: the FTAP (attainable-gains cone ⟹ the EMM), the coherent-risk representation (acceptance cone ⟹ representing density), and superhedging (super-replication cone ⟹ the price bound).

code.lean:
import MathFin.Foundations.ConvexDuality

/-- **Cone-separation root — the shared kernel of the convex-duality unification.**
    A closed convex cone `C ⊆ (ι → ℝ)` disjoint from the standard simplex admits a
    strictly-positive functional `q` that is `≤ 0` on `C`. One Hahn–Banach fact, three
    instances: the FTAP (apply to the attainable-gains cone — the separating `q` is the
    equivalent martingale measure), the coherent-risk representation (apply to the
    acceptance cone — `q` is a representing density), and superhedging (apply to the
    super-replication cone — `q` prices the bound). Re-exports
    `MathFin.exists_pos_separating_of_cone_disjoint_simplex`. -/
theorem convex_duality_root {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [Nonempty ι]
    (C : Set (ι → ℝ)) (hCconv : Convex ℝ C) (hCclosed : IsClosed C)
    (hCcone : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ C → ∀ ⦃c : ℝ⦄, 0 ≤ c → c • x ∈ C)
    (hdisj : Disjoint (stdSimplex ℝ ι) C) :
    ∃ q : ι → ℝ, (∀ i, 0 < q i) ∧ ∀ v ∈ C, ∑ i, q i * v i ≤ 0 :=
  MathFin.exists_pos_separating_of_cone_disjoint_simplex C hCconv hCclosed hCcone hdisj

metadata.reference: Convex-duality unification of asset pricing and risk (FTAP = coherent-risk representation = superhedging dual); finite-dimensional geometric Hahn–Banach
metadata.formalization_scope: Full re-export of the cone-separation root MathFin.exists_pos_separating_of_cone_disjoint_simplex (MathFin/Foundations/ConvexDuality.lean), the shared geometric kernel of the convex-duality unification. Generalizes the subspace separating-dual kernel exists_pos_dual_of_disjoint_stdSimplex (now re-derived from it) to a closed convex cone with a one-sided ≤ 0 bound — the form the acceptance cone (coherent risk) and the super-replication cone (superhedging) need, not just the FTAP gains cone. Proof: geometric_hahn_banach_compact_closed; the cone's nonnegative-scaling homogeneity upgrades the subspace's two-sided vanishing to a one-sided sign bound. No axioms beyond Mathlib defaults.

theorems.name: Fundamental Superhedging Bound
theorems.description: In a finite-state one-period market with excess-return matrix z, every martingale probability vector q (q ≥ 0, Σq = 1, every asset's excess return q-fair), in particular every equivalent martingale measure, prices a claim at most any of its super-replication costs: Σ_n q n Y n ≤ x whenever x plus some portfolio dominates Y in every state. The superhedging duality equality (superhedging price = supremum of EMM prices) is not proved.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Foundations.SuperhedgingDuality

open scoped BigOperators

/-- **Fundamental superhedging bound.** For an excess-return matrix `z`, any martingale
    probability vector `q` (`q ≥ 0`, `∑ q = 1`, every asset `q`-fair; in particular any
    equivalent martingale measure) and any cost-`x` portfolio `θ` super-replicating the claim
    `Y`, the `q`-price of `Y` is at most `x`. Re-exports `MathFin.emm_le_superReplication`. -/
theorem superhedging_emm_bound {M N : ℕ} (z : Fin M → Fin N → ℝ) (Y : Fin N → ℝ)
    {q : Fin N → ℝ} (hq : q ∈ MathFin.martingaleProbVectors z) {x : ℝ} {θ : Fin M → ℝ}
    (hsr : MathFin.SuperReplicates z Y x θ) :
    ∑ n, q n * Y n ≤ x :=
  MathFin.emm_le_superReplication z Y hq hsr

metadata.reference: H. Föllmer and A. Schied, Stochastic Finance: An Introduction in Discrete Time, 4th ed., de Gruyter (2016), §1.3 (superhedging and arbitrage-free prices)
metadata.formalization_scope: Full formal proof. Re-export of MathFin.emm_le_superReplication (MathFin/Foundations/SuperhedgingDuality.lean). SCOPE: q ranges over martingaleProbVectors z (q ≥ 0, possibly vanishing on some states), which contains every EMM (hasEMM_multi_state_iff_exists_pos_mem), so the statement is stronger than the EMM bound it is named after. Proof: q-weight the super-replication inequality; fairness (Σ_n q n z m n = 0) kills the portfolio term and Σq = 1 leaves x. Not proved: the strong-duality equality, which needs closedness of the finitely generated super-replication cone (Mathlib at this pin has PointedCone.DualFG but no Minkowski–Weyl).

theorems.name: Multi-State Single-Period FTAP (Biconditional)
theorems.description: No arbitrage ⟺ an equivalent martingale measure exists, in an arbitrary finite-state, finite-asset one-period market. The backward direction (no arbitrage ⟹ EMM) is finite-dimensional geometric Hahn–Banach separation of the attainable-payoff span from the standard simplex, completing the multi-state FTAP to a biconditional.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Foundations.FTAPMultiState

/-- **Multi-state single-period FTAP, biconditional** (Harrison–Pliska). In an
    arbitrary finite-state, finite-asset one-period market with excess-return
    matrix `z`, an equivalent martingale measure exists iff there is no
    arbitrage. The backward direction (no arbitrage ⟹ EMM) is finite-dimensional
    geometric Hahn–Banach separation of the attainable-payoff span from the
    standard simplex. Re-exports `MathFin.hasEMM_multi_iff_not_hasArbitrage`. -/
theorem ftap_single_period_complete {N M : ℕ} [NeZero N] (z : Fin M → Fin N → ℝ) :
    MathFin.HasEMM_multi_state z ↔ ¬ MathFin.HasArbitrage_multi_state z :=
  MathFin.hasEMM_multi_iff_not_hasArbitrage z

theorems.name: Finite-Ω Multi-Period FTAP (Harrison–Pliska)
theorems.description: On a finite full-support probability space with a filtration and an adapted scalar discounted price over a finite horizon, the market has no arbitrage ⟺ it admits an equivalent martingale measure. The finite case of Dalang–Morton–Willinger: backward via global separation of the attainable-gains subspace from the standard simplex, forward via martingale-transform telescoping.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Foundations.FTAPDiscrete

open MeasureTheory

/-- **Finite-Ω multi-period FTAP** (Harrison–Pliska; the finite case of
    Dalang–Morton–Willinger). On a finite full-support probability space with a
    filtration `𝓕` and an adapted scalar discounted price `S` over a finite
    horizon `T`, the market has no arbitrage iff it admits an equivalent
    martingale measure. Backward: the attainable-gains subspace misses the
    standard simplex under no arbitrage, so the separating hyperplane is the EMM.
    Forward: martingale-transform telescoping. Re-exports
    `MathFin.ftap_discrete`. -/
theorem ftap_discrete_complete {Ω : Type*} [Fintype Ω] [Nonempty Ω]
    {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} [MeasurableSingletonClass Ω] (𝓕 : Filtration ℕ mΩ)
    (P : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure P] (S : ℕ → Ω → ℝ) (T : ℕ)
    (hS : StronglyAdapted 𝓕 S) (hP : ∀ ω, 0 < P {ω}) :
    MathFin.NoArbitrage 𝓕 P S T ↔ ∃ Q, MathFin.IsEMM 𝓕 P S T Q :=
  MathFin.ftap_discrete 𝓕 P S T hS hP

theorems.name: General-Ω One-Period FTAP (Föllmer–Schied)
theorems.description: On an arbitrary probability space, a single scalar discounted excess return Y ∈ L⁰ admits no arbitrage ⟺ there is an equivalent martingale measure Q ~ P under which Y is integrable with E_Q[Y] = 0. The Föllmer–Schied / one-period Dalang–Morton–Willinger theorem — the measure-theoretic step beyond finite Ω: backward via a bounded-density reduction to L¹, the scalar no-arbitrage dichotomy, and a two-region balancing withDensity (no Hahn–Banach, no Kreps–Yan).

code.lean:
import MathFin.Foundations.FTAPOnePeriod

open MeasureTheory

/-- **General-Ω one-period FTAP** (Föllmer–Schied §1.2 / one-period
    Dalang–Morton–Willinger). For a single measurable scalar discounted excess
    return `Y` on an arbitrary probability space `(Ω, P)`, no arbitrage holds iff
    there is an equivalent martingale measure `Q ~ P` under which `Y` is
    integrable and `E_Q[Y] = 0`. Backward: a bounded-density reduction to `L¹`,
    the scalar no-arbitrage dichotomy, and a two-region balancing `withDensity`.
    Re-exports `MathFin.OnePeriod.ftap_one_period`. -/
theorem ftap_one_period_general {Ω : Type*} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω}
    (P : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure P] (Y : Ω → ℝ) (hY : Measurable Y) :
    MathFin.OnePeriod.NoArbitrage P Y ↔ ∃ Q, MathFin.OnePeriod.IsEMM P Y Q :=
  MathFin.OnePeriod.ftap_one_period P Y hY

metadata.reference: H. Föllmer and A. Schied, Stochastic Finance: An Introduction in Discrete Time, 4th ed., de Gruyter (2016), §1.2 (fundamental theorem of asset pricing, one period; the one-period case of Dalang–Morton–Willinger)
metadata.formalization_scope: Full biconditional NoArbitrage ⟺ ∃ EMM re-exported from MathFin/Foundations/FTAPOnePeriod.lean. Scope: one trading period, one scalar L⁰ return Y, arbitrary probability space (Ω, P). Backward direction (NA ⟹ EMM) is the elementary Föllmer–Schied route: a bounded strictly-positive density reduction (P̃ = P.withDensity of (1+|Y|)⁻¹/κ) making Y integrable, the scalar no-arbitrage dichotomy (a one-signed Y is killed by θ = ±1), and the two-region balancing withDensity Z = λ·𝟙_{Y≥0} + μ·𝟙_{Y<0} that re-weights up/down moves until Y is fair — no Hahn–Banach, no Kreps–Yan. Forward via E_Q[θ·Y] = 0. The general-Ω multi-period DMW (measurable selection) and the d-asset case are out of scope. No axioms beyond Mathlib defaults.

theorems.name: d-Asset One-Period FTAP (Esscher EMM, finite-dimensional market)
theorems.description: On an arbitrary probability space, for a ℝᵈ-valued discounted excess return Y, no arbitrage ⟺ there is an equivalent martingale measure Q ~ P with Y integrable and E_Q[Y] = 0 ∈ ℝᵈ — with no non-redundancy hypothesis. The backward direction is an explicit logistic-tilt construction (the softplus analogue of the Esscher measure, not the Esscher measure itself): minimise the smooth convex potential θ ↦ E[log(1 + exp⟪θ,Y⟫)]. The potential is constant along the gains kernel N = {θ : ⟪θ,Y⟫ = 0 a.e.} and coercive on its orthogonal complement Nᗮ, so a minimiser on Nᗮ is automatically global (redundant directions absorbed); its first-order condition E[Y·σ⟪θ₀,Y⟫] = 0 (σ logistic) yields a strictly-positive bounded density.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Foundations.FTAPOnePeriodVector

open MeasureTheory

/-- **d-asset one-period FTAP** (Föllmer–Schied §1.2, full). For a measurable
    `ℝᵈ`-valued discounted excess return `Y` on an arbitrary probability space and
    constant portfolios `θ ∈ ℝᵈ`, no arbitrage holds iff there is an equivalent martingale
    measure `Q ~ P` with `Y` integrable and `E_Q[Y] = 0` — with **no non-redundancy
    hypothesis** (redundant assets are absorbed by minimising the potential over the gains
    kernel's orthogonal complement). Backward: an explicit logistic-tilt EMM (the softplus
    analogue of the Esscher measure) from minimising `θ ↦ E[log(1+exp⟪θ,Y⟫)]`. Re-exports
    `MathFin.OnePeriodVector.ftap_one_period_vector` at `F = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)`. -/
theorem ftap_one_period_vector_market {Ω : Type*} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω}
    (P : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure P] {d : ℕ} (Y : Ω → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))
    (hY : Measurable Y) :
    MathFin.OnePeriodVector.NoArbitrage P Y ↔ ∃ Q, MathFin.OnePeriodVector.IsEMM P Y Q :=
  MathFin.OnePeriodVector.ftap_one_period_vector P Y hY

metadata.reference: d-asset one-period Fundamental Theorem of Asset Pricing (Föllmer–Schied §1.2; Esscher / minimal-entropy martingale measure)
metadata.formalization_scope: Honest derivation of the biconditional NoArbitrage ⟺ ∃ EMM re-exported from MathFin/Foundations/FTAPOnePeriodVector.lean, the FULL unrestricted one-period d-asset FTAP — no non-redundancy hypothesis. The MathFin theorem is stated for a discounted excess return valued in any finite-dimensional real inner-product space F (the ℝᵈ market is F = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)). Scope: one trading period, finite-dimensional market, trivial ℱ₀ (constant θ), arbitrary probability space. Backward direction (NA ⟹ EMM): minimise the smooth convex softplus potential θ ↦ ∫ log(1+exp⟪θ,Y⟫); it is constant along the gains kernel N = {θ : ⟪θ,Y⟫ = 0 a.e.} and, under no arbitrage, coercive on Nᗮ (via the unit-sphere minimum of g(θ)=∫⟪θ,Y⟫⁺ together with N ⊓ Nᗮ = ⊥), so a minimiser on Nᗮ exists and — because the potential is N-translation-invariant — is global over all of F; its first-order condition (differentiation under the integral) is ∫ Y·σ⟪θ₀,Y⟫ = 0, so z = σ⟪θ₀,Y⟫ ∈ (0,1) is a strictly-positive bounded fair density and Q = P.withDensity(z/∫z) is the EMM; integrability is dropped by a bounded-density reduction P̃ = P.withDensity((1+‖Y‖)⁻¹/κ). Redundant assets are thereby absorbed (no quotient by the gains kernel or measurable selection needed). No Hahn–Banach, no L⁰-cone closedness, no measurable selection. Only the general-Ω multi-period DMW remains out of scope. No axioms beyond Mathlib defaults.

theorems.name: Change of Numéraire (Price Invariance)
theorems.description: Given a pricing measure Q for the money-market numéraire B and a second strictly-positive numéraire N, the numéraire measure Q^N (Radon–Nikodym density dQ^N/dQ = (N_T·B₀)/(N₀·B_T)) reprices every terminal claim X consistently: N₀·E^{Q^N}[X/N_T] = B₀·E^Q[X/B_T]. This is the abstract change-of-numéraire theorem — the shared backbone of the library's concrete numéraire changes (the Black–Scholes stock numéraire, the exchange-option second-asset numéraire, the Garman forward/annuity normal form).

code.lean:
import MathFin.Foundations.Numeraire

open MeasureTheory

/-- **Change of numéraire — price is numéraire-invariant.**
Given a pricing measure `Q` for the money-market numéraire `B` and a second
strictly-positive numéraire `N`, the numéraire measure
`Q^N = numeraireMeasure Q B_T N_T B₀ N₀` (density `dQ^N/dQ = (N_T·B₀)/(N₀·B_T)`)
reprices every terminal claim `X` consistently:

  `N₀·𝔼^{Q^N}[X/N_T] = B₀·𝔼^Q[X/B_T]`.

The proof is a one-line density cancellation, and needs no integrability
hypothesis. This is the abstract backbone of the library's concrete numéraire
changes (the BS stock numéraire, the exchange-option second-asset numéraire, the
Garman forward/annuity numéraires). Re-exports `MathFin.changeOfNumeraire`. -/
theorem change_of_numeraire {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (Q : Measure Ω)
    (X BT NT : Ω → ℝ) (B0 N0 : ℝ)
    (hNTmeas : Measurable NT) (hBTmeas : Measurable BT)
    (hNTpos : ∀ ω, 0 < NT ω) (hBTpos : ∀ ω, 0 < BT ω) (hB0 : 0 ≤ B0) (hN0 : 0 < N0) :
    N0 * ∫ ω, X ω / NT ω ∂(MathFin.numeraireMeasure Q BT NT B0 N0)
      = B0 * ∫ ω, X ω / BT ω ∂Q :=
  MathFin.changeOfNumeraire X hNTmeas hBTmeas hNTpos hBTpos hB0 hN0

metadata.reference: Change of numéraire (Geman–El Karoui–Rochet); numéraire-invariance of arbitrage-free prices
metadata.formalization_scope: Full re-export of MathFin.changeOfNumeraire (MathFin/Foundations/Numeraire.lean): N₀·E^{Q^N}[X/N_T] = B₀·E^Q[X/B_T] where Q^N = Q.withDensity((N_T·B₀)/(N₀·B_T)). The identity is a pure measure-transport fact (integral_withDensity_eq_integral_toReal_smul) plus scalar cancellation of N_T — it holds for every claim X with NO integrability or square-integrability hypothesis, needing only strict positivity of the two numéraires. Companion numeraireMeasure_isProbabilityMeasure shows Q^N is a probability measure under the tradeability/normalization condition E^Q[N_T/B_T] = N₀/B₀ (N/B a Q-martingale). The abstract backbone is CONSUMED by the Black–Scholes stock numéraire: stockNumeraireMeasure_eq_numeraireMeasure (MathFin/BlackScholes/StockNumeraire.lean) exhibits dQ^(S)/dQ = e^{−rT}·S_T/S₀ as the instance B_T = e^{rT}, B₀ = 1, N = S. No axioms beyond Mathlib defaults.

theorems.name: Two-State FTAP Biconditional
theorems.description: In a one-period, one-asset market with two states and excess returns z_up, z_down, an equivalent martingale measure (q_up, q_down > 0, q_up + q_down = 1, q_up·z_up + q_down·z_down = 0) exists iff there is no arbitrage (no position θ with θ·z_up, θ·z_down ≥ 0 and one of them > 0). Proved as the N = 2, M = 1 case of the multi-state FTAP: the two-state EMM and arbitrage notions are shown equivalent to the multi-state ones for the matrix (z_up, z_down).

code.lean:
import MathFin.Foundations.FTAPMultiState

/-- **Two-state FTAP biconditional.** In a one-period, one-asset, two-state market with
    excess returns `z_up`, `z_down`, an equivalent martingale measure exists iff there is no
    arbitrage. The `N = 2`, `M = 1` case of the multi-state FTAP. Re-exports
    `MathFin.hasEMM_two_state_iff_not_hasArbitrage`. -/
theorem ftap_two_state_iff (z_up z_down : ℝ) :
    MathFin.HasEMM_two_state z_up z_down ↔ ¬ MathFin.HasArbitrage_two_state z_up z_down :=
  MathFin.hasEMM_two_state_iff_not_hasArbitrage z_up z_down

SCOPE: one period, one asset, two states; the EMM and arbitrage notions are those of MathFin/Foundations/FTAPTwoState.lean, proved equal to the multi-state ones at N = 2, M = 1 (hasEMM_two_state_iff_multi, hasArbitrage_two_state_iff_multi); the biconditional is then hasEMM_multi_iff_not_hasArbitrage (separation of the payoff span from the simplex). No hypotheses beyond the two real excess returns.

theorems.name: Finite-State EMM as a One-Period Equivalent Martingale Measure
theorems.description: For a one-period market with N states and M assets (excess-return matrix z) and any probability P on the N states that charges every state, a strictly positive probability vector q pricing every asset's excess return at zero exists iff there is a probability measure Q ~ P on the states under which the ℝᴹ-valued return vector is integrable with Q-mean zero. Derived by composing the finite-state FTAP (separation), a proved equivalence between matrix arbitrage and measure-theoretic arbitrage on Fin N, and the general-Ω vector FTAP (softplus construction), so the two independent FTAP proofs are shown to agree on finite state spaces.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Foundations.FTAPMultiState

open MeasureTheory

/-- **The finite-state EMM is the one-period EMM on the state space.** For any probability `P`
    on `Fin N` charging every state, an EMM vector for the excess-return matrix `z` exists iff
    some `Q ~ P` makes the `ℝᴹ`-valued return vector `multiStateReturn z` integrable with
    `E_Q[multiStateReturn z] = 0`. Re-exports `MathFin.hasEMM_multi_state_iff_exists_isEMM`. -/
theorem ftap_multi_state_measure_form {N M : ℕ} [NeZero N] (z : Fin M → Fin N → ℝ)
    (P : Measure (Fin N)) [IsProbabilityMeasure P] (hP : ∀ i, P {i} ≠ 0) :
    MathFin.HasEMM_multi_state z ↔
      ∃ Q, MathFin.OnePeriodVector.IsEMM P (MathFin.multiStateReturn z) Q :=
  MathFin.hasEMM_multi_state_iff_exists_isEMM z P hP

metadata.reference: H. Föllmer and A. Schied, Stochastic Finance: An Introduction in Discrete Time, 4th ed., de Gruyter (2016), §1.2 (fundamental theorem of asset pricing, one period)
metadata.formalization_scope: Full formal proof. Re-export of MathFin.hasEMM_multi_state_iff_exists_isEMM (MathFin/Foundations/FTAPMultiState.lean). SCOPE: finite state space Fin N with its discrete σ-algebra, any probability P with P {i} ≠ 0 for every state, returns as the EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin M)-valued map multiStateReturn z. The equivalence is derived, not constructed: hasEMM_multi_iff_not_hasArbitrage, hasArbitrage_multi_state_iff_not_noArbitrage (proved directly: P-a.e. is everywhere, and the payoff is an inner product), and OnePeriodVector.ftap_one_period_vector. The explicit correspondence q i = Q {i} is not stated.

theorems.name: Discrete-Time EMM at Horizon One Is the One-Period EMM
theorems.description: On a finite probability space with a filtration whose initial σ-algebra is trivial (𝓕 0 = ⊥) and an adapted scalar discounted price S, a measure Q is an equivalent martingale measure of the discrete-time market at horizon 1 iff it is an equivalent martingale measure of the one-period market for the excess return S 1 − S 0 (Q ~ P, E_Q[S 1 − S 0] = 0). The one-step martingale condition S 0 = E_Q[S 1 | 𝓕 0] becomes E_Q[S 1 − S 0] = 0 because S 0 is a constant and conditioning on ⊥ is expectation.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Foundations.FTAPDiscrete

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory

/-- **At horizon one the discrete-time EMM is the one-period EMM.** With trivial initial
    information `𝓕 0 = ⊥` and `S` adapted on a finite space, `Q` is an EMM of the one-step
    market iff it is an EMM of the one-period market for `S 1 − S 0`. Re-exports
    `MathFin.isEMM_one_iff_onePeriod`. -/
theorem discrete_emm_horizon_one {Ω : Type*} [Fintype Ω] {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω}
    [MeasurableSingletonClass Ω] (𝓕 : Filtration ℕ mΩ) (P : Measure Ω) (S : ℕ → Ω → ℝ)
    (hS : StronglyAdapted 𝓕 S) (h0 : 𝓕 0 = ⊥) (Q : Measure Ω) :
    MathFin.IsEMM 𝓕 P S 1 Q ↔ MathFin.OnePeriod.IsEMM P (S 1 - S 0) Q :=
  MathFin.isEMM_one_iff_onePeriod 𝓕 P S hS h0

metadata.reference: H. Föllmer and A. Schied, Stochastic Finance: An Introduction in Discrete Time, 4th ed., de Gruyter (2016), §1.2 (one-period model) and §5.2 (multi-period arbitrage and martingale measures)
metadata.formalization_scope: Full formal proof. Re-export of MathFin.isEMM_one_iff_onePeriod (MathFin/Foundations/FTAPDiscrete.lean). SCOPE: finite Ω, horizon T = 1, trivial 𝓕 0, scalar adapted price. The companion MathFin.noArbitrage_one_iff_onePeriod (same file, needs only 𝓕 0 = ⊥) identifies the no-arbitrage conditions; it is not part of this entry's statement. Longer horizons are not reduced to one-period markets here.

theorems.name: A Continuous-Time EMM Sampled Is a Discrete-Time EMM
theorems.description: If Q is an equivalent martingale measure for a scalar discounted price S in continuous time (Q ~ P and S a Q-martingale for a filtration 𝓕 indexed by ℝ≥0), then for any monotone schedule t 0 ≤ t 1 ≤ ⋯ and any horizon T, Q is an equivalent martingale measure in the finite-horizon discrete-time sense for the sampled price n ↦ S (t n) and the sampled filtration n ↦ 𝓕 (t n). General Ω. One direction only, and the discrete-time FTAP itself still needs a finite Ω.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Foundations.FTAPDiscrete

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
open scoped NNReal

/-- **A continuous-time EMM, sampled along a monotone schedule, is a discrete-time EMM** for
    the sampled price and filtration, at every finite horizon. Re-exports
    `MathFin.ContinuousMarket.IsEMM.sampled`. -/
theorem continuous_emm_sampled {Ω : Type*} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {P : Measure Ω}
    {𝓕 : Filtration ℝ≥0 mΩ} {S : ℝ≥0 → Ω → ℝ} {Q : Measure Ω}
    (h : MathFin.ContinuousMarket.IsEMM (P := P) (𝓕 := 𝓕) S Q)
    {t : ℕ → ℝ≥0} (ht : Monotone t) (T : ℕ) :
    MathFin.IsEMM (MathFin.ContinuousMarket.sampledFiltration 𝓕 ht) P (fun n ↦ S (t n)) T Q :=
  h.sampled ht T

metadata.reference: S. E. Shreve, Stochastic Calculus for Finance II: Continuous-Time Models, Springer (2004), §5.4 (fundamental theorems of asset pricing); H. Föllmer and A. Schied, Stochastic Finance: An Introduction in Discrete Time, 4th ed., de Gruyter (2016), §5.2
metadata.formalization_scope: Full formal proof. Re-export of MathFin.ContinuousMarket.IsEMM.sampled (MathFin/Foundations/FTAPDiscrete.lean), built on martingale_comp_monotone (MathFin/Foundations/ContinuousMarket.lean). SCOPE: scalar price (F = ℝ), arbitrary probability space, any monotone schedule and horizon. Not claimed: the converse (a measure that is a discrete EMM along every schedule need not make S adapted at all times), and any discrete-time no-arbitrage conclusion for non-finite Ω (ftap_discrete assumes a finite full-support space).

theorems.name: Triangle No-Arbitrage Is the Cross-Rate Identity
theorems.description: For three currencies with positive rates S_AB, S_BC (S_XY = units of Y per unit of X) and any S_CA, the three frictionless conversion trades A→B, B→C, C→A allow no arbitrage (no real combination whose net holding is non-negative in every currency and positive in one) iff S_AB·S_BC·S_CA = 1. No-arbitrage is the multi-state FTAP's notion with the currencies as coordinates; the forward direction uses the FTAP's separation half, the reverse prices with the currency values (S_AB·S_BC, S_BC, 1). Reverse trades are at the reciprocal rate; bid–ask spreads and transaction costs are not modelled.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Foundations.TriangleArbitrage

/-- **Triangle no-arbitrage is the cross-rate identity.** For positive `S_AB`, `S_BC`, the three
    frictionless conversion trades allow no arbitrage iff `S_AB · S_BC · S_CA = 1`. Re-exports
    `MathFin.triangleNoArb_iff`. -/
theorem triangle_no_arbitrage_iff_cross_rate {S_AB S_BC S_CA : ℝ} (hab : 0 < S_AB)
    (hbc : 0 < S_BC) :
    ¬ MathFin.HasArbitrage_multi_state (MathFin.triangleTrades S_AB S_BC S_CA) ↔
      S_AB * S_BC * S_CA = 1 :=
  MathFin.triangleNoArb_iff hab hbc

metadata.reference: Y. Aiba, N. Hatano, H. Takayasu, K. Marumo, T. Shimizu, Triangular arbitrage as an interaction among foreign exchange rates, Physica A 310 (2002) 467–479 (the rate product); H. Föllmer and A. Schied, Stochastic Finance: An Introduction in Discrete Time, 4th ed., de Gruyter (2016), §1.2

SCOPE: frictionless market of three conversion trades (triangleTrades), any real multiple of each trade allowed; arbitrage is HasArbitrage_multi_state over the currency coordinates. Positivity of S_AB and S_BC is used only for the reverse direction; prod_eq_one_of_triangleNoArb gives the forward direction for any signs. Not modelled: bid–ask spreads, transaction costs, position limits.

theorems.name: Law of One Price for Martingale Probability Vectors
theorems.description: In a finite-state one-period market with excess-return matrix z, every martingale probability vector q (q ≥ 0, Σq = 1, every asset's excess return q-fair; not necessarily strictly positive) prices a replicable claim at its replication cost: if Y n = x + Σ_m θ_m z m n in every state n, then Σ_n q n Y n = x.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Foundations.SuperhedgingDuality

open scoped BigOperators

/-- **Law of one price.** Every martingale probability vector prices a replicable claim at its
    replication cost. Re-exports `MathFin.martingalePrice_eq_of_replicates`. -/
theorem replicable_claim_martingale_price {M N : ℕ} (z : Fin M → Fin N → ℝ) {Y : Fin N → ℝ}
    {q : Fin N → ℝ} (hq : q ∈ MathFin.martingaleProbVectors z) {x : ℝ} {θ : Fin M → ℝ}
    (hrep : ∀ n, Y n = x + ∑ m, θ m * z m n) :
    ∑ n, q n * Y n = x :=
  MathFin.martingalePrice_eq_of_replicates z hq hrep

metadata.reference: H. Föllmer and A. Schied, Stochastic Finance: An Introduction in Discrete Time, 4th ed., de Gruyter (2016), §1.3 (arbitrage-free prices of attainable claims)
metadata.formalization_scope: Full formal proof. Re-export of MathFin.martingalePrice_eq_of_replicates (MathFin/Foundations/SuperhedgingDuality.lean). SCOPE: finite states and assets, exact replication Y = x + θ·z, q ranging over all martingale probability vectors (EMMs are the strictly positive ones). Proof: emm_le_superReplication applied to (x, θ) for Y and to (−x, −θ) for −Y.

theorems.name: Super-Replication Costs Are Bounded Below by an EMM Price
theorems.description: In a finite-state one-period market with at least one state and no arbitrage, there is a strictly positive martingale probability vector q (an equivalent martingale measure) such that, for every claim Y, every super-replication cost x (x plus some portfolio dominating Y in every state) is at least the q-price Σ_n q n Y n. So no claim's superhedging price is −∞. The superhedging duality equality (superhedging price = supremum of EMM prices) is not proved.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Foundations.SuperhedgingDuality

open scoped BigOperators

/-- **Under no arbitrage, one EMM price bounds every super-replication cost from below.**
    Re-exports `MathFin.exists_pos_price_le_superReplication`. -/
theorem superhedging_bounded_below_of_no_arbitrage {M N : ℕ} [NeZero N]
    (z : Fin M → Fin N → ℝ) (hNA : ¬ MathFin.HasArbitrage_multi_state z) :
    ∃ q ∈ MathFin.martingaleProbVectors z, (∀ n, 0 < q n) ∧
      ∀ (Y : Fin N → ℝ) (x : ℝ) (θ : Fin M → ℝ),
        MathFin.SuperReplicates z Y x θ → ∑ n, q n * Y n ≤ x :=
  MathFin.exists_pos_price_le_superReplication z hNA

Not proved: the reverse inequality / superhedging duality equality, which needs closedness of the finitely generated super-replication cone (absent from Mathlib at this pin); nonemptiness of the set of super-replication costs is not stated.

theorems.name: Covered Interest Parity from No-Arbitrage
theorems.description: In a finite-state market with state prices q and terminal spot S_T (domestic per foreign), pricing the domestic zero-coupon bond at e^{−r_d T} and the foreign zero-coupon bond, held in domestic currency, at S·e^{−r_f T}: the forward contract paying S_T − F has zero value iff F = S·e^{(r_d − r_f)T}.

code.lean:
import MathFin.FixedIncome.FxForwardParity

open MathFin

/-- **Covered interest parity.** -/
theorem covered_interest_parity_thm {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (q S_T : ι → ℝ)
    (S r_d r_f T F : ℝ)
    (h_dom : ∑ i ∈ s, q i = Real.exp (-(r_d * T)))
    (h_for : ∑ i ∈ s, q i * S_T i = S * Real.exp (-(r_f * T))) :
    ∑ i ∈ s, q i * (S_T i - F) = 0 ↔ F = S * Real.exp ((r_d - r_f) * T) :=
  covered_interest_parity s q S_T S r_d r_f T F h_dom h_for

theorems.name: Uncovered Interest Parity under the Domestic Risk-Neutral Measure
theorems.description: Under the Garman–Kohlhagen hypothesis (terminal spot S·exp((r_d − r_f − σ²/2)T + σ√T·Z) with Z standard normal under Q, S, K, σ, T > 0), the risk-neutral expected terminal spot is E_Q[S_T] = S·e^{(r_d − r_f)T}, the covered-parity forward. This is the risk-neutral form of uncovered interest parity; the same equation under the physical measure is not claimed.

code.lean:
import MathFin.FixedIncome.FxForwardParity

open MathFin MeasureTheory

/-- **Uncovered interest parity, risk-neutral form.** -/
theorem uncovered_interest_parity_thm {Ω : Type*} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω}
    {Q : Measure Ω} [IsProbabilityMeasure Q] {S K r_d r_f σ T : ℝ} {Z : Ω → ℝ}
    (h : BSCallHyp Q S K (r_d - r_f) σ T Z) :
    ∫ ω, bsTerminal S (r_d - r_f) σ T (Z ω) ∂Q = fxForward S r_d r_f T :=
  uncovered_interest_parity h

Re-export of MathFin.uncovered_interest_parity (MathFin/FixedIncome/FxForwardParity.lean), which is expected_terminal_eq_forward (MathFin/BlackScholes/Forward.lean, the Gaussian MGF) at drift r_d − r_f, the hypothesis of garman_kohlhagen_call_formula. theorems.name: Covered and Uncovered Interest Parity Agree
theorems.description: If a finite-state market (domestic bond at e^{−r_d T}, foreign bond in domestic currency at S·e^{−r_f T}) prices the forward S_T − F to zero, and the Garman–Kohlhagen hypothesis holds with the same spot S and rates, then F is the risk-neutral expected terminal spot E_Q[S_T]: the covered-parity forward equals the risk-neutral uncovered-parity expectation.

code.lean:
import MathFin.FixedIncome.FxForwardParity

open MathFin MeasureTheory

/-- **Covered and uncovered parity agree.** -/
theorem covered_eq_uncovered_interest_parity_thm {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (q S_T : ι → ℝ)
    {Ω : Type*} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {Q : Measure Ω} [IsProbabilityMeasure Q]
    {S K r_d r_f σ T F : ℝ} {Z : Ω → ℝ}
    (h_dom : ∑ i ∈ s, q i = Real.exp (-(r_d * T)))
    (h_for : ∑ i ∈ s, q i * S_T i = S * Real.exp (-(r_f * T)))
    (hF : ∑ i ∈ s, q i * (S_T i - F) = 0) (h : BSCallHyp Q S K (r_d - r_f) σ T Z) :
    F = ∫ ω, bsTerminal S (r_d - r_f) σ T (Z ω) ∂Q :=
  covered_eq_uncovered_interest_parity s q S_T h_dom h_for hF h
